title: Set 306

sentences.ko: 위층 집에 어린 남자애가 둘 있는데, 진짜 매일 아침 여섯 시만 되면 뛰어다니기 시작해. 애들이니까 뭐라고 하기도 좀 그렇긴 한데, 한 달 가까이 여섯 시 넘어서까지 자 본 적이 없어.
sentences.text: The family upstairs has two little boys, and I swear they start running laps at six every morning. I don't even want to complain, because they're just kids, but I haven't slept past six in like a month.

alts.text: Upstairs there's these two little boys who basically do laps every single morning at six. I'm not gonna complain, they're just kids, but I haven't slept past six in like a month.

The family living above us has two young sons, and I am fairly certain they begin running laps at six o'clock every morning. I do not wish to complain, as they are only children, but I have not slept past six in approximately a month.

sentences.note: **I swear** 는 진짜야, 내 말 믿어 하고 힘줘 말할 때 붙이는 말이에요. **slept past six** 는 여섯 시를 넘겨서까지 잤다는 뜻이고, **in like a month** 의 like 는 대충 그 정도라는 느낌을 더해 줘요.

sentences.ko: 우리 집 3월에 계약 끝나는데 월세를 200달러 올린대. 아니 뭐, 좀 더 외곽으로 가면 싼 데 구할 수 있을 것 같긴 한데, 그러면 편도로 한 시간씩 운전해야 하잖아. 그래서 솔직히 그럴 가치가 있는지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: Our lease is up in March and they're raising the rent by two hundred dollars. I mean, we could probably find something cheaper farther out, but then I'd be driving an hour each way, so I honestly can't tell if it's worth it.

alts.text: Lease is up in March and they're bumping the rent two hundred bucks. We could probably find a cheaper place farther out, but then it's an hour each way in the car, so I really dunno if it's worth it.

Our lease ends in March, and the landlord is increasing the rent by two hundred dollars. We could likely find a less expensive place farther from the city, but I would then be driving an hour in each direction, so I genuinely cannot determine whether it would be worthwhile.

sentences.note: **Our lease is up** 는 임대 계약이 끝난다는 말이에요. **each way** 는 편도로, 가는 데 한 번 오는 데 한 번씩이라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 딸이 책 하나만 더 읽어 달래더니, 다음엔 물 달라고 하고, 그다음엔 진짜 중요한 할 말이 있다는 거야. 들어 보니까 7월에 본 강아지 얘기였어. 겨우 잠들었을 땐 너무 지쳐서 저녁 먹을 힘도 없더라.
sentences.text: My daughter wanted one more story, then some water, then she had to tell me something really important, which turned out to be about a dog she saw in July. By the time she finally fell asleep, I was too tired to even eat dinner.

alts.text: First it was one more story, then water, then she just had to tell me something super important, and it was about some dog she saw back in July. Once she finally conked out, I was too wiped to even eat dinner.

My daughter asked for one more story, then a glass of water, and then said she needed to tell me something very important, which turned out to concern a dog she had seen in July. By the time she finally fell asleep, I was too exhausted even to eat dinner.

sentences.note: **turned out to be** 는 알고 보니 ~였다는 뜻이에요. **By the time** 은 ~할 즈음에는, ~했을 때는 이미 라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 우리 개가 청소기 무서워한다고 내가 얘기했던가? 꺼져 있어도 청소기 보고 짖어서, 이제는 산책 나갈 때까지 기다렸다가 청소해야 돼.
sentences.text: Did I tell you our dog's scared of the vacuum? He barks at it even when it's turned off, so now I have to wait until he's out on a walk before I can clean anything.

alts.text: Oh, did I mention our dog's terrified of the vacuum? He'll bark at it even when it's off, so I've gotta wait till he's out on a walk to clean anything.
Have I mentioned that our dog is afraid of the vacuum cleaner? He barks at it even when it is switched off, so I now have to wait until he is out on a walk before I can clean anything.

sentences.note: **Did I tell you** 는 내가 말했던가? 하면서 새 얘기를 꺼낼 때 써요. **out on a walk** 는 산책 나가 있는 상태를 말해요.

sentences.ko: 드디어 무릎 검사받았는데, 별거 아니래. 콘크리트 바닥에서 뛰지만 않으면 된대. 다행이긴 한데, 나는 일주일 내내 수술해야 되는 줄 알았다니까.
sentences.text: I finally got my knee checked out, and apparently it's nothing serious, I just have to stop running on concrete. Which is great, but I spent a whole week convinced I was going to need surgery.

alts.text: Got my knee looked at finally, and turns out it's nothing serious, I just gotta quit running on concrete. Great news, but I spent a whole week sure I'd need surgery.

I finally had my knee examined, and it appears to be nothing serious; I simply need to stop running on concrete. That is very good news, but I spent an entire week convinced that I would require surgery.

sentences.note: **got my knee checked out** 은 무릎을 병원에서 봐 달라고 했다는 뜻이에요. **convinced** 는 그렇다고 굳게 믿고 있었다는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

reviewed: 2번 casual 의 prob 은 문자로 칠 때 쓰는 줄임말이라 말로는 안 해서 probably 로 바꿈
4번 formal 의 until he has been taken for a walk 는 산책을 다녀온 뒤처럼 읽혀 뜻이 달라지므로 until he is out on a walk 로 고침
4번 한국어 산책 나갔을 때까지 기다렸다가 가 어색해서 산책 나갈 때까지 기다렸다가 로 고침
5번 한국어 끝의 알고 있었잖아 는 듣는 사람도 이미 안다는 말투라 상황에 안 맞아서 알았다니까 로 고침
